title: 2026-10-26 — A sidecar entry payload lands through `rec.py amend`, never appended to a file

data.head: ## 2026-10-26 — A sidecar entry payload lands through `rec.py amend`, never appended to a file

body: The entry writers' `{doc}-entries.md` is a payload of `@amendment` records, and `rec.py amend --root . --doc {doc} --file {run_dir}/{doc}-entries.md` (`--dry-run` first) lands it as rows after the sidecar's last, the store placing each entry and its separation itself; nothing is appended to a sidecar file by hand or by script. [corrected 2026-11-04: the records DB's S5 retired `splice.py append` and `--blank-before` — the installed `splice.py` has `summary` · `index` · `delete` · `section` only — and the wrap of 2026-11-04-linux-and-macos-parity landed its 19 entries through `rec.py amend`, each read back by its id.]

- 2026-11-04: When a test's OS reader (a `ps` keyword, a `/proc` file, a system call) fails only on a CI runner the host cannot reproduce, first make the test's failure carry what the reader returned — its exit and both streams — and push that alone; change or re-gate the reader only on that reading, never on a guess at the runner's form.

The plan's expected amendment places it beside the repository's scripts as the operator pass's per-OS JUnit reading. It is never a CI step, a pre-push stage or a harness command.

Test-only, root test support: tests/support/frozen.rs holds the Frozen guard, one twin per OS (Unix sends kill -STOP, polls ps -o stat= until T, and sends kill -CONT on drop; Windows attaches a debugger with kill-on-exit off and detaches on drop), the one shared way a test freezes a wrapper so its heartbeat goes stale.

Measured at ci#41915621814: macOS ps has no sigignore keyword (its keywords include blocked, sigmask, pending and sig), so a process's ignored-signal mask has no ps reader on macOS, and a test that reads it is gated to Linux with that reason.

A test-only parity chunk: no file under src/, crates/*/src/, schemas/, plugin/, fixtures/, .github/, Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock moved (the preservation guard read clean, 13 files changed, all allowed), and no product symbol, IPC method, env var, socket or CI step changed.
It added tests/support/frozen.rs (the shared Frozen guard, moved out of tests/cli_instance_state.rs), tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs (a census that names every OS-gated test with its reason: 52 functions and 7 files, 59 GATES rows, reason constants UNIX_MODES, UNIX_STATUSLINE and NO_PEER_PID), and scripts/junit-os-sets.py (an operator-only per-OS JUnit reader that uses python stdlib and the host gh, never a CI step).
It ungated run_child_ends_when_its_wrapper_is_terminated to every OS, landed the Unix outer-PTY witness of the dim stale row in viola list, and added one reason line to each of ten OS-gated tests that had none, several of them owner-only mode and strict-modes tests.
It measured that macOS ps has no keyword for the ignored-signal mask, so the fake-agent hangup case stays Linux-only and reads ps -o sigignore= in place of /proc SigIgn; the fake agent's SIGHUP-ignoring exit itself is unchanged.
CI on the final sha (ci#41918694243) was green, 15/15 checks across the three OS legs, secret scan included. Per-OS JUnit: 48 cases run on ubuntu-latest and not on macos-latest, 43 of them through the macOS no-peer-pid carve-out and 5 Linux-only for a named reason.
The ci nextest profile's 20 s kill line went from 26 to 27 binaries. That is a test-runner setting, not a security control.

It passes on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.

run_child_ends_when_its_wrapper_is_terminated (tests/run_cli.rs) runs on every OS. On Windows it terminates the wrapper with OpenProcess and TerminateProcess; on Unix with kill -KILL of the wrapper pid, its exit asserted. It then asserts that the child, read by pid and start time from snapshot_data, is gone within WITHIN.

fake_agent_exit_outlives_a_hangup_that_lands_while_it_exits (tests/cli_fake_agent.rs) is cfg(target_os = linux). It reads the agent's SIGHUP disposition through ps -o sigignore= -p <pid>, and its failure carries ps's exit and both streams. It does not run on macos-latest because macOS ps has no keyword that prints the ignored-signal mask (measured at ci#41915621814). That gate was the operator's ruling. The fake agent's SIGHUP-ignoring exit stays shared Unix code and is witnessed on Linux only.

tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs is the census of OS-gated tests. Its GATES table has a file, test, gate and reason for each row. The census walks every .rs directly under tests/ and in each crates/*/tests/. It counts a leading #![cfg(...)], and a test function whose attribute run holds #[test], #[rstest] or #[tokio::test] together with a cfg or cfg_attr whose predicate names windows, unix or target_os outside string values. Its faults check works both ways: an unnamed gate, and a row that no longer stands. Its tests are os_gated_tests_are_each_named_with_their_reason, gates_table_rows_are_unique and census_finds_an_unnamed_gate_and_passes_a_named_one, the last a self-check over eight planted cases.
The OS-gated census reads 52 OS-gated test functions and 7 gated files, which make 59 GATES rows. The count includes cfg_attr case rows, for example the two functions in tests/hook_fail_open.rs.
contract_os_gated_tests is a root contract_ test binary. It is auto-discovered with no [[test]] table and is selected by the E2E layer's regex, so it runs under run --e2e in suite nextest-e2e.

The ci profile's stamped-home override filter in .config/nextest.toml:24 is the 20 s kill: slow-timeout with period 10s and terminate-after 2. It names 27 binaries, binary(run_cli) among them, placed after binary(path1_run_start). The count is the number of binary(...) names on that filter line.

scripts/junit-os-sets.py --run <id> is an operator-pass instrument and never a CI step. It uses python 3 stdlib only. It downloads junit-windows-2025, junit-macos-latest and junit-ubuntu-latest with gh run download into a temp dir removed on exit. It prints each OS's cases, failed and skipped counts, then the sorted classname::name sets for ubuntu-not-macos, macos-not-ubuntu, windows-not-ubuntu and ubuntu-not-windows. It exits 0, 1 (a report missing or unparsable, named) or 2 (usage).

The per-OS JUnit at ci#41918694243 (cbdd3874, green 15/15) reads windows-2025 3386, macos-latest 3412 and ubuntu-latest 3458 cases, 0 failed and 0 skipped. Its set differences are ubuntu-not-macos 48, macos-not-ubuntu 2, windows-not-ubuntu 88 and ubuntu-not-windows 160. The 48 split as 43 cases of the macOS no-peer-pid carve-out plus 5 Linux-only cases, each with a named reason.
